theorem_obligations.intent: If complete guard evaluates false, execution returns `guardFalse` with the unchanged state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For all states s and instructions i, if evalGuard s i.guard = some false then execCnotB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem cnotB32_exec_guard_false_no_state_change (s : MachineState) (i : CnotB32Instruction) (h : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) : execCnotB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)
hypotheses: h : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Example states can realize false guard (e.g. `Guard.atPos` with pred false); theorem asserts non-trivial no-op outcome, not merely function extensionality.
strength_risks: Do not weaken h to `evalGuard ... = some v` or omit completeness of the false case.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execCnotB32 and rewrite with h; reduce to the `some false` branch.

theorem_obligations.intent: On true guard and resolvable source, destination register receives `cnotB32` of the source value in the executed post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If evalGuard is `some true`, destination is a register r, and evalSource is `some va`, then execCnotB32 produces an executed state whose destination register r equals `cnotB32 va`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem cnotB32_exec_true_guard_writes_cnot_result (s : MachineState) (i : CnotB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va : U32) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va) : ∃ s', execCnotB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (cnotB32 va)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va
theorem_obligations.conclusion: ∃ s', execCnotB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (cnotB32 va)
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Concrete states with non-missing guard/source force this branch and produce a non-trivial written value (`0` becomes `1`; non-zero becomes `0`).
strength_risks: Destination bit-bucket case intentionally excluded here via explicit `Destination.reg` precondition.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split evalGuard with hguard, split evalSource with ha, and simplify updateDestination at index r after rewriting hd.

theorem_obligations.intent: Characterize exactly when partiality (`none`) occurs in bounded executable semantics.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: execCnotB32 s i = none iff guard is missing, or guard is true and source is missing.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem cnotB32_exec_none_iff_missing_guard_or_true_source (s : MachineState) (i : CnotB32Instruction) : execCnotB32 s i = none ↔ (evalGuard s i.guard = none) ∨ (evalGuard s i.guard = some true ∧ evalSource s i.a = none)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: execCnotB32 s i = none ↔ (evalGuard s i.guard = none) ∨ (evalGuard s i.guard = some true ∧ evalSource s i.a = none)
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: States with missing predicate produce no result, and states with true guard but missing source also produce no result; both directions are behaviorally meaningful.
strength_risks: Do not include guard=false in the none condition; false guard should return guard-false outcome.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on evalGuard, then on evalSource when in the true case, matching execCnotB32 cases directly.
